summary: Session 89 live-code infrastructure audit. Four local root fixes are premise-verified: certified Pressure/Breach evidence can currently exceed 100% under contradictory stage chronology; Worker game IDs rely on an untested random brute-force helper; the production service worker uses a permanent cache namespace and can delete unrelated origin caches; and the canonical startup brief renders unknown runway as green, ignores live compliance fields, emits S?, placeholder test/deploy rows, and labels a fresh render as a prior closeout. External launch observations remain a truthful NO-GO corridor. The registry type correction remains externally owned after Studio Ops rejected the exact Ark delta because type is outside its safe allowlist.

items.title: Make certified Pressure-to-Breach evidence mathematically admissible
items.why: CertifiedLoopEvidenceStore counts each stage independently. A contradictory certified payload can therefore report Breach without Pressure, decisive delivery before Breach, victory before delivery, or conversion above 100%, and the aggregate surface will still label it certified-match-result.
items.recipe: Create one pure chronology projector for Pressure, Breach, decisive delivery, and victory; require a complete prefix and nondecreasing ticks; reject malformed timelines before persistence; keep absent future stages valid; prove all adversarial gaps/orderings, process/PostgreSQL parity, replay behavior, and 0-100 conversion bounds.

L1.recipe: Clamp conversion percentages and add one malformed fixture.

L2.recipe: Validate stage presence and chronology before aggregation.

L3.recipe: Extract a pure certified timeline authority, reject before persistence, and prove adversarial/process/PostgreSQL parity plus bounded summaries.

executionLog: Added a pure CertifiedLoopTimeline authority that accepts only a complete nondecreasing Pressure → Breach → decisive delivery → victory prefix and emits typed failure codes.

CertifiedLoopEvidenceStore now rejects gaps, time reversal, fractional ticks, and invalid intervals before process-local or PostgreSQL persistence; 13 focused tests and the direct TypeScript gate pass.

items.title: Make the canonical startup brief refuse confident unknowns and placeholders
items.why: The freshly rendered Session 89 brief marks unknown runway green, ignores PROJECT_STATUS compliance 49/49, emits LAST SESSION (S?) with Tests/Deploy placeholders, warns that HUMAN PRESSURE is missing, and stamps the render as Session 88 closeout. This is the founder-facing source agents are required to trust.
items.recipe: Represent unknown runway explicitly and never green; fall back to live PROJECT_STATUS compliance evidence; parse both Session N and SN summaries; wrap rather than silently amputate the shipped headline; render source-derived test/deploy facts and an explicit zero-pressure block; stamp render time and source-closeout session separately; extend canonical helper and validator tests so S?, placeholders, confident unknowns, and provenance conflation fail.

L1.recipe: Fix Session N parsing and unknown-runway icon classification.

L2.recipe: Use live compliance/test/deploy fields and always render HUMAN PRESSURE.

L3.recipe: Separate render/source provenance, wrap summaries, and add fail-closed golden invariants for every former placeholder/confident-unknown shape.

executionLog: Canonical brief blocks now parse both Session N and SN, wrap the shipped headline, and render direct suite/deploy evidence instead of S? and placeholders.

The renderer separates render time from source-closeout session, treats unknown runway as unverified, consumes PROJECT_STATUS compliance fallback, always renders HUMAN PRESSURE, and passes focused tests plus the canonical validator.

items.title: Replace Worker game-ID roulette with a tested bounded preimage authority
items.why: Worker.ts labels generateGameIdForWorker a hack and performs up to 1,000 opaque full-ID guesses. Matchmaking and rematch creation both depend on it, it is private and untested, collision retry is split at call sites, and failure has no typed reason.
items.recipe: Extract an eight-character, alphabet-preserving worker-routed GameID authority that performs bounded suffix preimage search against the canonical config workerIndex, accepts a collision predicate, preserves legacy ID shape and entropy, returns typed exhaustion evidence, and is shared by matchmaking/rematch paths. Add deterministic multi-worker, collision, malformed-generator, and exhaustion tests plus a Worker composition contract.

L1.recipe: Extract and unit-test the existing bounded random loop.

L2.recipe: Use deterministic suffix preimage search with an injected collision predicate.

L3.recipe: Preserve the exact public ID contract, share one typed authority across both consumers, prove adversarial exhaustion, and ratchet composition.

executionLog: Extracted WorkerGameId as one eight-character, alphabet-preserving suffix-preimage authority with seed and candidate bounds, typed failure evidence, and an injected collision predicate.
Rematch and matchmaking now share the authority; deterministic 16-worker routing, collision, malformed seed, exhaustion, rematch, composition, and TypeScript gates pass.

items.title: Bind offline cache ownership to the deployed service-worker release
items.why: The production service worker uses permanent vaultfront-v1, deletes every other cache on the origin during activation, and caches any /assets/ response without an explicit same-origin ownership check. New releases retain old asset weight and a shared origin could lose caches owned by another surface.
items.recipe: Derive a release namespace from the hashed service-worker script URL; scope cleanup to prior VaultFront-owned namespaces only; resolve pre-cache URLs from registration scope; cache only successful same-origin immutable assets; preserve network-first navigation and API/WebSocket exclusions; expose pure cache-policy helpers with adversarial cross-origin, unrelated-cache, base-path, and release-rotation tests; bind the service worker contract into Pages verification.

L1.recipe: Change the cache name and restrict deletion to a VaultFront prefix.

L2.recipe: Use hashed-script release identity, registration scope, and same-origin asset policy.

L3.recipe: Extract and adversarially test the cache policy, verify release rotation, and add the exact service-worker invariant to the deployed Pages artifact contract.

executionLog: Extracted a pure release-bound cache policy: the hashed compiled worker URL owns the cache namespace, registration scope owns pre-cache URLs, and cleanup cannot touch caches outside the VaultFront prefix.

Replaced the non-executable inlined TypeScript data URL with a real hashed sw-*.js production asset; 14 focused tests, TypeScript, the Pages build, and the 10/10 service-worker-aware deploy contract pass.
